title: Which of two phone plans is cheaper over a year
summary: Plan B wins below 1.875 GB of monthly overage; compare the full year.

blocks.heading: How often do you go over?
blocks.body: For these fictional plans, A costs $540 a year. B starts at $360, then adds $8 for every GB above its included allowance. B wins if your total overage for the year stays below 22.5 GB.

blocks.heading: Try your usage pattern
blocks.caption: Example prices. Overage means usage beyond B’s allowance, not total data use. Fractional GB are billed proportionally in this example; taxes and fees are excluded.

blocks.heading: An average can hide an expensive month
blocks.body: One month with 12 GB of overage and eleven months with none costs B $456 for the year. The comparison uses the sum of monthly overages; unused allowance does not cancel another month’s overage.

blocks.heading: Try a year
blocks.prompt: Your last 12 bills total 24 GB of overage. Which plan is cheaper?
blocks.explanation: B = 12 × $30 + 24 × $8 = $552. A saves $12. Check coverage, included allowance and billing increments before treating the fictional price comparison as a buying decision.
